svg.title: Thirty Days to an Evidence-Ready Bid Desk
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-first-thirty-days-roadmap; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: Thirty Days to an Evidence-Ready Bid Desk; subtitle: Build operating readiness without assuming an award in the first month.; chapter number: 12; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Numeric values identify milestone end days. The sprint establishes service scope, systems, and pursuit discipline; the canonical time to first deal remains 6–18 months. Client awards, signed engagements, recognized fees, and collected cash are separate events.; caption: Advance on completed evidence: a service charter, an opportunity matrix, a tested submission workflow, and a dated pursuit plan.; stages: label: Days 1-7; value: Define one service niche and fee structure; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Select one supplier segment and initial jurisdiction. Draft deliverables, exclusions, pricing, and client responsibilities; complete the four statutory checks. Produce a service charter, conflict register, and startup cash plan with explicit spending limits.; label: Days 8-14; value: Build alerts, calendars, and opportunity evidence; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Configure SAM.gov saved searches and relevant municipal portal monitoring. Review ten actual notices, record mandatory requirements and amendments, and assign calendar owners. Produce a dated opportunity matrix with documented reasons for pursuing or rejecting each notice.; label: Days 15-21; value: Test supplier qualification and submission controls; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Conduct five capability interviews and document delivery constraints. Run a mock submission using a public notice, without transmitting a bid. Test attachment naming, deadline time zones, client signoff, access recovery, and receipt retention.; label: Days 22-30; value: Launch measured outreach and cash review; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Issue service proposals only to qualified prospects with reviewed structures. Publish a ninety-day pursuit calendar and weekly receivables review. Record observed cohort conversion separately from the illustrative funnel; do not count outreach, bids, or client awards as earned fees.

rect.title: label: Days 1-7; value: Define one service niche and fee structure; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Select one supplier segment and initial jurisdiction. Draft deliverables, exclusions, pricing, and client responsibilities; complete the four statutory checks. Produce a service charter, conflict register, and startup cash plan with explicit spending limits.

text.title: Define one service niche and fee structure
text.tspan: Define one service niche and fee

rect.title: label: Days 8-14; value: Build alerts, calendars, and opportunity evidence; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Configure SAM.gov saved searches and relevant municipal portal monitoring. Review ten actual notices, record mandatory requirements and amendments, and assign calendar owners. Produce a dated opportunity matrix with documented reasons for pursuing or rejecting each notice.

text.title: Build alerts, calendars, and opportunity evidence

rect.title: label: Days 15-21; value: Test supplier qualification and submission controls; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Conduct five capability interviews and document delivery constraints. Run a mock submission using a public notice, without transmitting a bid. Test attachment naming, deadline time zones, client signoff, access recovery, and receipt retention.

text.title: Test supplier qualification and submission controls

rect.title: label: Days 22-30; value: Launch measured outreach and cash review; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Issue service proposals only to qualified prospects with reviewed structures. Publish a ninety-day pursuit calendar and weekly receivables review. Record observed cohort conversion separately from the illustrative funnel; do not count outreach, bids, or client awards as earned fees.

text.title: Launch measured outreach and cash review

Assumptions: Numeric values identify milestone end days. The sprint establishes service scope, systems, and pursuit discipline; the canonical time to first deal remains 6–18 months. Client awards, signed engagements, recognized fees, and collected cash are separate events.
